q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of fruit jam per kg?
title: Fruit jam carbon footprint per kg
short: Add fruit pulp, sugar and pectin per kg of jam with supplier figures, then the steam for boiling and concentration, filling and the jars or bottles. Divide the plant's energy by kg packed; glass jars can weigh close to the jam itself.
audience: Jam, jelly and fruit spread makers

ul: Fruit pulp or fruit by weight.
Glass jars, PET jars or sachets with caps.
Steam jacketed kettles or vacuum pans.

p: Report per kg of jam, with the pack listed separately so a glass and a plastic pack can be compared.

example.title: Worked example: fruit jam unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 43,400 / 100,000 = 0.434 kg CO2 per kg
Add fruit, sugar and jars for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
